data.narrative:
Elroy Air, a Series B autonomous drones company, is valued at $800M post-money on $116M total raised. The broader Drones & Autonomous sector comprises eight private peers—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—with no public comparables identified.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-later-stage funding rounds, yielding $1.5B. Peer-median methodology is inapplicable; while six same-sector peers exist, insufficient narrow-set datapoints at identical or adjacent stages preclude reliable median construction. A broader all-sector median would introduce undue noise given the specialized nature of autonomous systems valuations.

The analysis supports a triangulated range of $1.3B to $1.7B, with $1.5B as the point estimate. This range reflects stage-typical progression mechanics but carries material uncertainty given the single-method foundation. Key risks to valuation include execution on autonomous capability roadmaps, regulatory pathway clarity for commercial deployment, and capital intensity relative to revenue traction—none of which can be quantified from available data. A more robust triangulation would require additional same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable transactions in autonomous systems to validate or adjust the stage-progression baseline.
